content.comment_body: I developed a project using [product_name] with a custom web page and sent data to the cloud. On AWS IoT, my data changes as expected. I uploaded my custom web page using [product_name] editor [version_no]. The page appears correctly on AWS Elastic Beanstalk, with a green status, but the environment message is: Tomcat 8.5 with Java 8 running on 64-bit Amazon Linux/[version_no] Deprecated. The web page looks fine in the cloud but isn't connected to [product_name]. It worked successfully a few times, but after making some changes in the editor and re-uploading to the cloud, the system stopped working. I tried creating a new environment and a new [product_name] resource, but nothing helped.

I'm glad my issue was resolved in the meantime. I created a new IAM user in AWS, and everything started functioning as intended. However, I've noticed that some versions of the app don't work properly after being uploaded—the cause is not clear. I usually transfer the new version into the same cloud environment and have even tested in a fresh environment, but the results are the same: the web application is online, but dynamic data does not update. In summary: deploying applications to the cloud is unpredictable, although investors require stable operation.

You should upgrade your [product_name] editor to [version_no] and use this updated version to upload your project to AWS again. There have been changes in the AWS background environment, so using the upgraded editor should help your project adapt to these updates.

analysis.insight_summary: Users face inconsistent connectivity and data synchronization when deploying custom web pages made with [product_name] editor to AWS cloud environments. While deployment and basic page display work, reliable dynamic data transfer between devices and cloud-hosted web apps remains difficult. Upgrading the editor or adjusting to AWS background changes are recurring challenges.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect smooth and dependable synchronization of dynamic data between their devices and cloud-hosted web applications. They want to be able to redeploy updates without issues and avoid frequent manual troubleshooting.
